commit.message:
fix(diff): disclose mixed-quote renames and prevent adjacent-file scope masking (#8285)

With core.quotePath=true (the loader's pin) git quotes each diff --git
header path independently, so an ASCII-to-Unicode rename arrives as
a/src/lib.rs "b/src/<quoted>.rs". parse_git_old_path only recognized the
unquoted " b/" boundary, so the old path was lost, the exact rename-pair
match in handle_rename_metadata failed, and the renamed file silently
vanished from scope; a separately parseable section (e.g. a Cargo.toml
[lib] path edit) then masked the missing scope with a complete-looking
result, and an isolated pure-rename section was refused as malformed_diff.

The old-path reader now recognizes the independently quoted destination
boundary before its existing unquoted boundary. An unquoted old path
cannot contain a quote (git would have quoted the whole path), so the
quoted boundary is unambiguous. Confinement, adversarial-path controls,
and the loader quoting pin are unchanged.

Red -> green evidence (predicates 1-3 of #7795):
- path.rs::parse_git_old_path_pairs_each_destination_quoting_layout
- parse.rs::metadata_registers_mixed_quote_pure_rename_under_new_path
- parse.rs::metadata_registers_mixed_quote_edited_rename_under_new_path
- cli_smoke mixed_quote_rename.rs: five literal layouts x pure/edited
  with native NUL name-status inventory pins, adjacent-file masking, and
  isolated pure-section disclosure

Closes #7795

commit.message:
fix(rust): credit a test pinning a returned element's field through a borrowed alias (#7858) (#8309)

* fix(rust): credit a test pinning a returned element's field through a borrowed alias (#7858)

A test that binds `let r = &rows[k];` and asserts `r.f` against a literal
reads the same element the inline `rows[k].f` read does. The alias must be a
plain immutable shared borrow of the receiver (or a direct owner call) at the
probed literal index, named like neither the owner nor the receiver, and bound
once. RIPR-SPEC-0225 decision 9 records the rule.

commit.message:
feat(first-run): time the prebuilt release-archive install route (#8321)

* feat(first-run): time the prebuilt release-archive install route (#5311)

`cargo xtask first-run --install-archive VERSION` downloads the host's
server archive, verifies its SHA-256 sidecar, extracts only the root
`ripr` into the walk's own directory and walks that executable by path.

assert_eq!(k * (r == Err(E::Bad)) as u32, n) read exact_error_variant/strong
although the other factor may be zero. Cap arithmetic over an integer-cast
test and another non-literal term (RIPR-SPEC-0231 rule 1).

its own non-literal partner and read only boolean spellings as literals, so
`(r == Err(E::Bad)) as u32 + 1` against `2` capped. Require a non-literal
term other than the test, and read numeric literals as literals.

commit.message:
fix(python): read a bound match pattern from its own function scope (#8356)

* fix(python): read a bound match pattern from its own function scope

The name lookup scanned the whole file, so a same-named binding in another
function could supply or hide the pattern, and a parameter named like the
pattern was read as an assignment elsewhere. Read the enclosing function's
body plus module-level lines; refuse when the name is a parameter.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01RfN9skVT5954WH8jN1MTKd

* fix(python): parse the def signature by brackets and fall back for nested defs

Review findings on #8356: a '#' or ':' inside a default value ended the
signature early and hid body bindings; a nested def lost the outer
function's binding. Fall back to the whole file where scope is not modeled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01RfN9skVT5954WH8jN1MTKd

Graphite review on #8356: the nested-def fallback fired for every unittest

commit.message:
feat(orch): migrate orchestration consumers to selected-work portfolio basis (#1706 PR B) (#8325)

* feat(orch): task/result schemas migrate to selected-work basis (#1706)

#1633 consumer of #1706 delivery slice PR B: adds RIPR-SPEC-0269 and
xtask/src/work_result_identity.rs. Every committed WorkTaskResultV1 row
must bind the repository, the compiled portfolio-snapshot identity, the
basis head and the full RIPR-SPEC-0244 SelectedWorkIdentityV1 it extends;
the shared selection law engine runs inside the result check, never a
forked one. A result for another repository, portfolio snapshot,
issue/action, stale basis, unrecorded worktree or wrong exact head fails
stale/wrong-input with the exact recompile/reconcile route; an
evidence-free result fails as a claim-not-result; legacy
active-goal/current-work-item refs resolve read-only with migration
posture and grant no authority.

Adds cargo xtask work result check [--corpus <dir>] [--json], a five-
scenario committed corpus (14 pinned cases) reusing the RIPR-SPEC-0244
captured directories by reference, sha256-bound provenance, twelve tests,
and the spec/traceability/doc-artifact/catalog/fixture registrations.

Proof: cargo test -p xtask --bin xtask work_result_identity (12/12);
check-spec-format, check-spec-numbering, check-doc-index,
check-traceability, check-fixture-contracts, check-command-catalog,
check-output-contracts, check-changelog-fragments, check-static-language,
check-file-policy, check-local-context, check-no-panic-family,
check-allow-attributes all pass; clippy -D warnings clean; fmt clean.

Refs #1706

* feat(orch): durable claims migrate to selected-work basis (#1706)

#1635/#1647 consumer of #1706 delivery slice PR B: adds RIPR-SPEC-0270
and xtask/src/work_claim_identity.rs. Every committed WorkClaimV1 row
binds one selected issue/work item/action and the exact portfolio basis;
the shared RIPR-SPEC-0244 selection law engine runs inside the claim
check, never a forked one. The schema has no priority, default-campaign,
agent-assignment, CI-wait or progress fields, so claiming one item never
asserts repository-wide priority. A stale basis keeps the claim recorded
as stale_requires_reconcile - reconcile, never release or takeover; a
duplicate claim id, one worktree serving two selections and one selection
double-claimed each fail with the exact law/route pair while the
occupying claim stays active. Legacy active-goal/current-work-item refs
resolve read-only with migration posture and grant no authority.

Adds cargo xtask work claim check [--corpus <dir>] [--json], a five-
scenario committed corpus (9 pinned cases) reusing the RIPR-SPEC-0244
captured directories by reference, sha256-bound provenance under the
work_claim_identity_provenance.v1 schema, thirteen tests, and the
spec/traceability/doc-artifact/catalog/fixture registrations.

Proof: cargo test -p xtask --bin xtask work_claim_identity (13/13),
work_result_identity (12/12), work_selection_identity (24/24);
check-spec-format, check-spec-numbering, check-doc-index,
check-traceability, check-fixture-contracts, check-command-catalog,
check-output-contracts, check-changelog-fragments, check-static-language,
check-file-policy, check-local-context, check-no-panic-family,
check-allow-attributes all pass; clippy -D warnings clean; fmt clean.

Refs #1706

* feat(orch): wave planning migrates to selected-work basis (#1706)

#1634 consumer of #1706 delivery slice PR B: adds RIPR-SPEC-0271 and
xtask/src/work_wave_identity.rs. Every committed WorkWavePlanV1 row
consumes the complete selected candidate set and partitions it into
waves over the explicit resource vocabulary campaign-record:<id>,
portfolio-schema, spec-ledger, output-contract:<id>, issue:<n>, pr:<n>
and worktree:<path>; the shared RIPR-SPEC-0244 selection law engine runs
over each embedded selection, never a forked one. The retired generic
active-goal resource and every non-explicit shape fail closed with the
explicit-vocabulary route; portfolio-schema and spec-ledger are read-only
shareable references that never serialize unrelated work; shared
exclusive resources, over-capacity waves, unassigned candidates and
stale bases each fail with the exact recompile/reconcile route; disjoint
cross-campaign waves are admitted.

Adds cargo xtask work wave check [--corpus <dir>] [--json], a six-
scenario committed corpus (7 pinned cases) reusing the RIPR-SPEC-0244
captured directories by reference, sha256-bound provenance under the
work_wave_identity_provenance.v1 schema, thirteen tests, and the
spec/traceability/doc-artifact/catalog/fixture registrations.

Proof: cargo test -p xtask --bin xtask work_wave_identity (13/13),
work_claim_identity (13/13), work_result_identity (12/12),
work_selection_identity (24/24); check-spec-format, check-spec-numbering,
check-doc-index, check-traceability, check-fixture-contracts,
check-command-catalog, check-output-contracts, check-changelog-fragments,
check-static-language, check-file-policy, check-local-context,
check-no-panic-family, check-allow-attributes all pass; clippy -D
warnings clean; fmt clean.

Refs #1706

* feat(orch): context packets migrate to selected-work basis (#1706)

#1632 consumer of #1706 delivery slice PR B: adds RIPR-SPEC-0272 and
xtask/src/work_context_identity.rs. Every committed WorkContextPacketV1 row
must bind the repository, the compiled portfolio-snapshot identity, the
basis head and the full RIPR-SPEC-0244 SelectedWorkIdentityV1 it compiles
context for; the shared selection law engine runs inside the context
check, never a forked one. The delegation scope is a closed bounded
vocabulary (selected_work_only / selected_work_plus_relevant_overflow, no
repository-wide scope) and every carried context/overflow reference must
stay relevant to the bound selection, so campaign references remain
context, never permission and a standalone issue with no campaign
placement still compiles a valid packet. An unresolvable legacy ref, an
irrelevant carried reference, unbounded overflow, an evidence-free packet,
a wrong repository or a stale basis fails with the exact
recompile/reconcile route; legacy active-goal/current-work-item refs
resolve read-only with migration posture and grant no authority.

Adds cargo xtask work context check [--corpus <dir>] [--json], a six-
scenario committed corpus (11 pinned cases) reusing the RIPR-SPEC-0244
captured directories and selection packets by reference, sha256-bound
provenance, fourteen tests, and the spec/traceability/doc-artifact/
catalog/fixture registrations.

check-spec-format, check-spec-numbering, check-doc-index,
check-traceability, check-fixture-contracts, check-command-catalog,

check-file-policy, check-local-context, check-no-panic-family,
check-allow-attributes all pass; clippy -D warnings clean; fmt clean.

Refs #1706

* feat(orch): root synthesis migrates to selected-work basis (#1706)

#1636 consumer of #1706 delivery slice PR B: adds RIPR-SPEC-0273 and
xtask/src/work_synthesis_identity.rs. Every committed WorkSynthesisV1 row
must bind the repository, the compiled portfolio-snapshot identity, the
basis head and the full RIPR-SPEC-0244 SelectedWorkIdentityV1 it reports
on; the shared selection law engine runs inside the synthesis check, never
a forked one. The reported transition must match the selected action, so a
synthesis cannot silently report a different transition; every uncovered
or contradicted acceptance row must be named in the contradictions list,
so a synthesis can never hide a gap behind a green row; a reported
campaign ref outside the bound selection's campaign refs is a silent

commit.message:
perf(xtask): build covered_by test targets in one cargo call and optimize the syntax stack in dev (#8397)

check-file-policy warmed xtask's and ripr's test targets with separate
cargo calls that serialize on the target-dir lock (~2m + ~2m cold). One
combined --no-run call lets Cargo schedule them together; failures are
ignored there and still surface in each selector's own spawn.

Unoptimized rowan/ra_ap_syntax dominated the source scans. Optimizing that
small stack drops check-static-language 156s->3s, check-public-api and
source-role-authority 20s->3s, check-no-panic-family 32s->8s warm.

@@ -0,0 +1,10 @@
+<!-- section: Added -->
+- `cargo xtask work burndown check` validates committed burn-down rows
+  against the compiled work-portfolio basis: every burn-down binds the
+  repository, portfolio-snapshot identity, basis head and the
+  selected-work identity it tracks, reusing the RIPR-SPEC-0244 selection
+  law engine; completion derives from issue/spec acceptance,
+  implementation slices, PRs and exact-head review/proof evidence rows,
+  campaign and work-item records are plan context only and a `complete`
+  burn-down over an open or stale row fails with the reconcile route, and
+  legacy goal/work-item refs resolve read-only with no authority (#1706).

@@ -0,0 +1,11 @@
+<!-- section: Added -->
+- `cargo xtask work adapter check` validates committed Codex delegation
+  rows against the compiled work-portfolio basis: every delegation binds
+  the repository, portfolio-snapshot identity, basis head and the full
+  selected-work identity it delegates, one closed project role and one
+  closed flow stage, the subagent consumes the selected-work context
+  packet plus relevant overflow and never re-reads the portfolio,
+  write-capable builder delegations require a prepared claim or isolated
+  worktree, subagents never claim, and a wrong repository, snapshot, basis
+  or legacy authority attempt fails with exact recompile/reconcile routes
+  (#1706).

@@ -0,0 +1,13 @@
+<!-- section: Added -->
+- `cargo xtask work context check` validates committed context/work-item
+  packet rows against the compiled work-portfolio basis: every packet binds
+  the repository, portfolio-snapshot identity, basis head and the
+  selected-work identity it compiles context for, reusing the
+  RIPR-SPEC-0244 selection law engine; the delegation scope is a closed
+  bounded vocabulary and every carried context/overflow reference must stay
+  relevant to the bound selection (campaign references are context, never
+  permission), a standalone issue with no campaign placement still
+  compiles a valid packet, and an unresolvable legacy ref, an irrelevant
+  reference, unbounded overflow, an evidence-free packet, a wrong
+  repository or a stale basis fails with exact recompile/reconcile routes
+  (#1706).

@@ -0,0 +1,7 @@
+<!-- section: Added -->
+- `cargo xtask work claim check` validates committed durable-claim rows
+  against the compiled work-portfolio basis: every claim binds one selected
+  issue/action and the exact basis, a stale basis keeps the claim recorded
+  for reconcile (never release or takeover), one worktree cannot serve two
+  selections and one selection cannot be double-claimed, and legacy
+  goal/work-item references resolve read-only with no authority (#1706).

@@ -0,0 +1,11 @@
+<!-- section: Added -->
+- `cargo xtask work intake check` validates committed issue-intake rows
+  against the compiled work-portfolio basis: every intake binds the
+  repository, portfolio-snapshot identity, basis head, current main and
+  one issue the captured portfolio records; campaign placement and
+  relevant campaigns must be recorded campaigns, but an out-of-campaign
+  issue may still qualify because placement stays a later root/planning
+  decision, open overlapping PRs and claims stay visible before any
+  mutation, and an empty contract set, an unknown issue, a wrong
+  repository or a legacy authority attempt fails with exact
+  recompile/reconcile routes (#1706).

@@ -0,0 +1,11 @@
+<!-- section: Added -->
+- `cargo xtask work plan check` validates committed plan rows against the
+  compiled work-portfolio basis: every plan binds the repository,
+  portfolio-snapshot identity, basis head and the full selected-work
+  identity it plans for, planning emits one closed disposition and is
+  read-only so a row that would replace or reorder the whole portfolio
+  fails visibly, campaign-targeting dispositions must name a recorded
+  campaign, a blocked disposition must name its blocker, a plan derived
+  from nothing is a claim, and a wrong repository, snapshot, basis or
+  legacy authority attempt fails with exact recompile/reconcile routes
+  (#1706).

@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+<!-- section: Added -->
+- `cargo xtask work synthesis check` validates committed root-synthesis
+  rows against the compiled work-portfolio basis: every synthesis binds
+  the repository, portfolio-snapshot identity, basis head and the
+  selected-work identity it reports on, reusing the RIPR-SPEC-0244
+  selection law engine; the reported transition must match the selected
+  action, every uncovered or contradicted acceptance row must be named in
+  the contradictions list so a synthesis can never hide a gap, a reported
+  campaign ref outside the bound selection's campaign refs is a silent
+  switch that fails, the schema has no field that could create another
+  selected issue, and legacy goal/work-item refs resolve read-only with no
+  authority (#1706).

@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+<!-- section: Added -->
+- `cargo xtask work result check` validates committed task-result rows
+  against the compiled work-portfolio basis: every result must bind the
+  repository, portfolio-snapshot identity, basis head and the selected-work
+  identity it extends, reusing the RIPR-SPEC-0244 selection law engine;
+  wrong repository, snapshot, issue/action, basis, worktree or head fails
+  stale/wrong-input with exact recompile/reconcile routes, evidence-free
+  results fail as claims, and legacy goal/work-item references resolve
+  read-only with no authority (#1706).

@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+<!-- section: Added -->
+- `cargo xtask work wave check` validates committed wave plans against the
+  compiled work-portfolio basis: every plan consumes the complete selected
+  candidate set and partitions it into waves over explicit resources
+  (`campaign-record:<id>`, `portfolio-schema`, `spec-ledger`,
+  `output-contract:<id>`, `issue:<n>`, `pr:<n>`, `worktree:<path>`); the
+  retired generic `active-goal` resource fails closed, shared exclusive
+  resources and over-capacity waves fail with exact reconcile routes, and
+  disjoint cross-campaign waves are admitted (#1706).

@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+<!-- section: Docs -->
+- The MCP guide shows how to register `ripr mcp --stdio` with Claude Code and Codex, notes that `ripr_refresh` analyzes committed edits only, and no longer says the server never prepares a repair when `ripr_prepare_repair` creates an in-memory transaction (https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr/issues/3092).

@@ -0,0 +1,4 @@
+<!-- section: Internal / CI -->
+- Gate-test corpus copies now remain owned through evaluation and are removed
+  after the last reader or a setup failure, preserving current-worktree fixture
+  bytes and hermetic evaluation roots (#3742).

@@ -0,0 +1,4 @@
+<!-- section: Fixed -->
+- `ripr doctor` on Windows no longer selects an interpreter-only PATHEXT entry
+  (`.PS1`, `.VBS`, `.JS`) ahead of a working `.exe` exporter; only suffixes
+  `CreateProcessW` can launch (`.COM`, `.EXE`, `.BAT`, `.CMD`) are tried (#5351).

@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+<!-- section: Changed -->
+- `ripr doctor`'s "Safe next action" line family (missing root, invalid
+  config, failed prerequisites, runnable first command) is now selected by
+  the canonical next-action decision instead of two duplicated state
+  ladders. Rendered text is unchanged (#6986, doctor slice).

@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+<!-- section: Changed -->
+- `ripr first-pr --check` now exits 2 when the current start-here packet records a blocked state (wrong root, missing or malformed artifacts), and `ripr help first-pr` documents the exit contract; write mode still exits 0 after composing the packet (#7373).

@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+<!-- section: Changed -->
+- The `ripr plus` indeterminate receipt warning and `ripr help plus` now say that no ripr command produces the missing complete test-efficiency measurement, candidate-binding and scope-disposition evidence yet (tracked in #7222), instead of ending at "inspect the source evidence" (#7375).

@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+<!-- section: Fixed -->
+- `ripr cache clear` now names the real directory in its symlink-alias refusal
+  through the shared `human_path` renderer, so a Windows drive-letter verbatim
+  prefix is stripped like `Cache dir:` and `Real dir:` (#7487). The refusal
+  itself stays fail-closed.

@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+<!-- section: Fixed -->
+- TypeScript and JavaScript: three rarer deleted-line owner headers are now recognised, so a type-only header edit keeps the deleted body line as base-side evidence on the live owner instead of dropping it: a typed binding whose type is a generic function with a type-parameter default (`const f: <T = string>(a: T) => void = …`), an anonymous default export (`export default function (`, `export default (x) => {`), and a class field named `get` or `set` (`get = (id) => {`). Base-side records stay out of counts, gates, cards and diagnostics (#7705).

@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+<!-- section: Fixed -->
+- A test that pins a returned array element's field through a borrowed alias of that element now credits the field instead of leaving a false gap (#7858).

@@ -0,0 +1,4 @@
+<!-- section: Fixed -->
+- Arithmetic over an integer-cast test and another non-literal term
+  (`assert_eq!(k * (r == Err(E::Bad)) as u32, n)`) no longer earns
+  `exact_error_variant`/strong credit (RIPR-SPEC-0231 rule 1; #8101).

@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+<!-- section: Fixed -->
+- A comparison or pattern compared with a non-literal side through the same
+  `Some(..)`, `Ok(..)` or `Err(..)` on both sides
+  (`assert_eq!(Some(r == Err(E::Bad)), Some(expected))`) no longer earns
+  `exact_error_variant`/strong credit (RIPR-SPEC-0231 rule 1; #8101).

@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+<!-- section: Changed -->
+- The default `ripr check` human output now uses plain language: the summary, triage state, finding digest, hidden list, and analysis-outcome line no longer leak snake_case schema tokens (such as `weakly_exposed` or `top_gap`). `--format human-full`, JSON, and `ripr explain` keep the full schema tokens unchanged (#8165).

@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+<!-- section: Fixed -->
+- A Rust test that expects a seeded collection after the owner call (`assert_eq!(p.log, vec![9])`) no longer credits a changed or deleted push into that collection as `exposed` when the owner can return before it (`if self.locked { return; }`, `?`, a panicking call). That test took the early exit, so the assertion only restates the seeded state and cannot tell the push apart from its mutants. An expectation containing the pushed value, or an owner that cannot exit early, keeps its strength (#8205).

@@ -0,0 +1,8 @@
+<!-- section: Added -->
+- `ripr doctor` now warns when git already tracks files under `target/ripr`,
+  even when `.gitignore` covers it: an ignore rule does not untrack reports
+  committed earlier, so `git add -A` kept refreshing them and `ripr check`
+  kept diffing them. The warning names `git rm --cached -r -- target/ripr`.
+  `doctor --json` carries it as the new `cache.artifact_tracking` field
+  (`untracked`, `not_checked`, or `tracked` with the warning), separate from
+  `cache.artifact_ignore` (#8276).

@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+<!-- section: Internal / CI -->
+- LSP lifecycle test servers use two Tokio scheduler workers each, preserving
+  multi-thread protocol checks while bounding inherited worker pools (#8283).

@@ -0,0 +1,4 @@
+<!-- section: Fixed -->
+- `ripr agent verify-execute --json` emits its existing typed response when the
+  selected root is missing or names a file, preserving exit `2` and root recovery
+  guidance without executing the packet or writing a result (#8284).

@@ -0,0 +1,4 @@
+<!-- section: Fixed -->
+- `ripr pilot` keeps restored vendor source and evidence excluded while its
+  changed checksum marker remains sparse. Warm-cache output refreshes population
+  comparability and preserves ordinary inventory reuse (#8288).

@@ -0,0 +1,4 @@
+<!-- section: Internal / CI -->
+- Stop unlocked package qualification when packaging, identity, extraction,
+  directory entry, or lockfile preparation fails, preserving the failing command's
+  status instead of continuing to a misleading successful check (#8330).

@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+<!-- section: Added -->
+- `ripr init --mcp` adds the ripr MCP server to the project's `.mcp.json` for Claude Code, keeping other servers and any existing `ripr` entry, and prints the `codex mcp add` command for Codex (https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr/issues/8331).

@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@

Set `resolve_tsconfig_paths = false` to keep aliased imports unresolved (RIPR-SPEC-0099 amendment, #8346).

@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+<!-- section: Fixed -->

+  archive: it downloads the host's server archive, verifies its SHA-256
+  sidecar, extracts `ripr` into the walk's own directory and runs that
+  executable, recording the route, asset, digest and acquisition time apart
+  from the source-install sample (#5311).

@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@

A failing exporter's own stderr is now part of the reported producer failure instead of being discarded (#8352).

+fn a_literal_none_match_checks_no_message_in_either_framework() -> Result<(), String> {
+    // #7849: `match=None` and `assertRaisesRegex(E, None)` disable message
+    // matching, so only the exception class is pinned. Exact patterns and an
+    // omitted `match=` keep their existing verdicts.
+    assert_ne!(
+        parse_class(
+            "def test_parse():\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=None):\n        parse(\"\")\n"
+        )?,
+        ExposureClass::Exposed
+    );
+    let unittest = |pattern: &str| {
+        classify(
+            PARSE,
+            3,
+            PARSE_OLD,
+            &test_module(
+                "import unittest\n\nfrom src.shop import parse",
+                &format!(
+                    "class ParseTest(unittest.TestCase):\n    def test_parse(self):\n        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, {pattern}):\n            parse(\"\")\n"
+                ),
+            ),
+        )
+    };
+    // A name bound exactly once to `None` reads as `None`.
+    assert_ne!(
+        parse_class(
+            "def test_parse():\n    pattern = None\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=pattern):\n        parse(\"\")\n"
+        )?,
+        ExposureClass::Exposed
+    );
+    // A second binding is not a single `None` assignment: the message
+    // stays checked.
+    assert_eq!(
+        parse_class(
+            "def test_parse():\n    pattern = None\n    pattern = \"empty\"\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=pattern):\n        parse(\"\")\n"
+        )?,
+        ExposureClass::Exposed
+    );
+    assert_ne!(unittest("None")?, ExposureClass::Exposed);
+    assert_ne!(unittest("expected_regex=None")?, ExposureClass::Exposed);
+    assert_eq!(unittest("\"empty\"")?, ExposureClass::Exposed);
+    Ok(())
+}

+        assert_ne!(parse_class(body)?, ExposureClass::Exposed, "{body}");
+        Ok(())

+    // A `#` inside a default string and a colon inside a default dict do not

+    broad(

+    broad(

+            .replace('\n', "\r\n"),
+    )?;
+    // A nested def keeps reading the enclosing function's binding.
+    broad(
+        "def test_parse():\n    pattern = \".*\"\n\n    def check():\n        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=pattern):\n            parse(\"\")\n\n    check()\n",
+    )?;
+    Ok(())

-# Proof-routing dry-run evidence (0.9.0 candidate)
-
-**Date:** 2026-06-10
-**Issue:** #1078 (P16 evidence collection)
-**Informs:** #1080 (P17 docs/spec routing), #1079 (P18 report/schema routing)
-**Source artifact:** generated from `cargo xtask proof route` over five representative merged PRs; raw working copy at `target/ripr/reports/p16-proof-route-evidence.md`.
-
-This packet answers the P16 question: across representative PR categories, what would proof routing have skipped, and would any skip have dropped a lane that carried real signal? Routing is **advisory-only** today (`proof_route.rs` hardcodes `routing_state = "advisory-report-only"`), so CI ran every lane and the skips are **counterfactual inferences**, not observed enforcement.
-
----
-
-## Explicit conclusions
-
-| Question | Answer |
-|----------|--------|
-| **P17 docs/spec routing safe to implement?** | **Yes — docs/markdown-only category only.** The single docs-only sample (#1063) is unambiguously safe; no other category clears. |
-| **P18 report/schema routing safe to implement?** | **Not yet.** xtask/report/schema (#1067) and release-like (#1069) read **ambiguous** (static-language + coverage skips have observable relevance). Requires the manifest fixes below first, then re-evidence. |
-| **Manifest/router fixes required before any code routing** | (1) **Uncovered lanes:** `rust`, `msrv`, `coverage`, `policy` are owned by no proof pack, so routing marks them skipped on every PR — they must be mapped onto the code packs or pinned unconditional before P18. (2) **Keep `static-language` unconditional** — it showed real relevance on static-output PRs. (3) **output-contracts lane gap** (#1079): the pack requires `goldens check` + `fixtures` but its lane does not run them. |
-| **Release proof remained protected?** | **Yes.** `release-package` (`never_routed = true`) never appeared in `skipped_lanes` on any PR; `release_proof_required = true` fired correctly on every release-surface PR (#1067, #1069, #1072). |
-| **Unknown surfaces remained conservative?** | **Partially — and this is why mixed/unknown is unsafe.** #1072 (touching `policy/proof-packs.toml`, an unmatched surface) correctly forced 7 required lanes incl. release proof, but the routed verdict still skips `rust`/`msrv`/`policy` because those lanes are unowned (see uncovered-lanes finding). Unknown-surface handling is not yet conservative enough for enforcement outside docs-only. |
-
-**Bottom line:** enable the docs/markdown-only skip in P17; do **not** enable any code/report/schema skip until the uncovered-lane and output-contracts manifest gaps are closed and re-evidenced.
-
----
-
-## The uncovered-lanes finding (key P18 prerequisite)
-
-The proof-pack manifest's `ci_lane` values cover only: `docs`, `static-language`, `output-contracts`, `traceability`, `routed-rust-small` (×2 packs), `vscode-e2e`, `release-readiness-proof`. The heavy/important CI lanes **`rust`, `msrv`, `coverage`, and `policy` are owned by no pack at all**, so `proof route` reports them `skipped (no_matched_surface)` on *every* PR — including pure Rust-code PRs (this is precisely why #1056 routed to require only `static-language`).
-
-Consequence for sequencing:
-- **Docs-only (P17) is unaffected:** a markdown PR legitimately needs none of `rust`/`msrv`/`coverage`/`policy`, so "skipping" them is correct.
-- **Any code/report routing (P18) is blocked** until those lanes are mapped onto the code packs (`analysis-fixture` / `xtask-report`) or pinned unconditional — otherwise enforcement would skip the real build/test/coverage lane on published Rust.
-
----
-
-## Sample
-
-| PR | Commit | Category | Changed files | Release proof required | Required lanes | Skipped lanes |
-|----|--------|----------|---------------|------------------------|----------------|---------------|
-| #1063 | 6affb336 | docs/markdown-only | 6 | false | `docs` | 25 |
-| #1056 | 5751cd8f | normal Rust code | 5 | false | `static-language` | 24 |
-| #1067 | f3b7a9fe | xtask/report/schema | 11 | true | `docs`, `routed-rust-small`, `release-readiness-proof` | 20 |
-| #1069 | 99eed4b7 | release-like | 7 | true | `docs`, `routed-rust-small`, `release-readiness-proof` | 20 |
-| #1072 | f932cb1f | mixed/unknown-surface | 7 | true | `docs`, `routed-rust-small`, `static-language`, `output-contracts`, `traceability`, `vscode-e2e`, `release-readiness-proof` | 18 |
-
-Sample strategy: all five are real merged PRs after #1070 (where P16 artifacts begin). No synthetic PRs were created. The `release-like` slot (#1069) touches `CHANGELOG.md` + xtask; no PR in this window touched `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`, so true version-bump release evidence should be confirmed against the source release PR (#1424) during Phase R rather than asserted here.
-
----
-
-## Routed-vs-actual per PR
-
-### #1063 — docs/markdown-only — **SAFE**
-Three markdown files (DOCUMENTATION.md, PROOF_ROUTING.md, ROADMAP.md); no Rust/policy/fixture/editor surface. `release_proof_required=false`. CI: `routed-rust-small` on CX43 SUCCESS, rust-tests-junit SUCCESS, rust-coverage SUCCESS, source-of-truth SUCCESS, cargo-deny SUCCESS, codecov/patch SUCCESS; `rust`/`msrv`/`vscode` independently skipped by CI. No failures. Every routed skip is a lane with no plausible failure mode on pure markdown.
-
-### #1056 — normal Rust code — **UNSAFE**
-Published-crate refactor (commands.rs, commands/pilot.rs). Routed to require only `static-language`, skipping `rust`/`routed-rust-small`/`coverage`. **codecov/patch FAILED**, confirming the coverage lane had real signal. Skipping build+test on a published Rust code-motion PR is a material gap.
-
-### #1067 — xtask/report/schema — **AMBIGUOUS**
-Introduces proof_route.rs (new static output) + CHANGELOG.md. Routed skips `static-language` (the gate validating static output) on the very PR adding static-output paths, and skips `coverage` where **codecov/patch FAILED**. xtask is unpublished (lowers rust-skip risk), but both skips have observable relevance → ambiguous.
-
-### #1069 — release-like — **AMBIGUOUS**
-Adds proof_route.rs rendering to pr-summary (437 new lines) + CHANGELOG.md. Same pattern as #1067: `static-language` and `coverage` skipped where codecov/patch FAILED and new static text was added. `release_proof_required=true` and `release-readiness-proof` required are correct, but the two skips have real relevance → ambiguous.
-
-### #1072 — mixed/unknown-surface — **UNSAFE**
-Modifies policy/proof-packs.toml + adds xtask validation (proof_preflight.rs, expanded proof_route.rs). Unknown surface correctly forced 7 required lanes incl. release proof, but still skips `rust`/`msrv`/`policy`. **cargo-deny and source-of-truth were CANCELLED** (in-flight, not passively skipped) on a PR hardening release-proof invariants — required signal did not complete. Unsafe.
-
----
-
-## Caveats
-
-1. **Advisory-only routing:** skips are counterfactual inferences; no skip was actually enforced.
-2. **Single sample per category:** a "safe" verdict could be accidentally safe. Docs-only should accrue more samples before broad confidence, though one clean sample plus the structural argument (markdown matches only `docs-spec`, `release_proof_required=false`) is adequate to *enable* the docs-only skip.
-3. **`routed-rust-small` multi-platform gap:** maps to several jobs (CX43/CPX42/CX53/GitHub-Hosted); typically only CX43 ran, so even the required lane lacked full multi-platform compile coverage.

-**Date**: 2026-06-12  
-**Scope**: TypeScript preview repair-packet actionability logic — enumerating every way a TS finding could be wrongly marked actionable (repair_packet_ready := true when unsafe) and stating the fail-closed invariants required to prevent each.

-## Executive Summary
-

-2. **Oracle Strength Floor**: oracle_strength >= Strong (exact value, not snapshot/smoke/mock-guess)
-3. **Related Test Ownership**: related test is owner-call-aware (not heuristic-only, not cross-package)
-4. **Verify Command Realism**: verify_command is framework-aware, not a guess (jest/vitest/bun/npm/pnpm/yarn)
-5. **Receipt Command Availability**: receipt_command exists and runs (not stubbed, not delegated to external provider)

-8. **No Mock/Snapshot as Discriminator**: mock-payload and snapshot-based oracles cannot be treated as actionable discriminators
-9. **Custom Matcher Rejection**: custom/unknown matchers must be advisory-only
-10. **No Guessed Repair Kind**: repair_kind must be derived from static analysis, not guessed from confidence score
-11. **No Line-Keyed Finding ID**: finding IDs must be content-addressed (probe:file:family:hash), not line numbers
-12. **No Unverifiable Assertion Shape**: assertion_shape must be concrete code, not prose or template variables
-13. **No Confidence Inflation**: oracle_confidence must not inflate for missing expected values
-14. **No Cross-Package Test Target**: test file must be in same package root as owner file (monorepo-aware)
-15. **No Unresolved Test Framework**: test framework must be detected (jest/vitest/bun, not guessed)

-## Detailed Failure Mode Enumeration

-## Testing Strategy
-
-### Unit Tests (Rust)
-- **oracle.rs**: 10+ tests for dynamic/literal expected values, async modifiers, error variants
-- **related_tests.rs**: 10+ tests for same_package_root, owner_call_relation, import verification, shadowing
-- **actionability.rs**: Tests for each actionability_category (static, observed, context, relation, shape, incomplete)
-- **package.rs**: Tests for verify_command generation per framework (jest, vitest, bun, node)
-- **validate_agent_gap_record_packet**: 15+ failure mode tests (missing receipt, bad projection, preview gate, etc.)
-
-### Integration Tests
-- E2E: Full TS finding → GapRecord → packet → agent execution
-- Monorepo: Test with multiple packages; reject cross-package relations
-- Cross-language: Inject external-language test as related; verify rejection
-- Dynamic matcher: Inject `expect(x).toBe(getSomeValue())`; verify rejection
-- Mock + snapshot: Inject both oracle types; verify advisory state
-
-### Adversarial Harness
-- Inject malformed GapRecords (empty receipt, template variables, broad edit surface)
-- Inject crafted TypeScript findings (fake oracle_strength, guessed framework)
-- Attempt to bypass invariants (set repair_packet_ready = true in JSON, bypass validation)
-- Measure: 0 false positives (no unsound packets), 0% over-emit rate
-
----
-
-## Conclusion
-
-**No TypeScript repair packet should be marked actionable (`repair_packet_ready = true`) unless ALL 20 fail-closed invariants hold.** Each invariant is a guard against a distinct failure mode. Violations must be caught early (Rust validation), reported clearly (evidence), and escalated to advisory-only status (safe fallback).
-
-**The cardinal principle**: A wrongly-emitted actionable packet (one that is NOT actually safe to delegate) is the cardinal sin. Erring on the side of caution — marking more findings advisory than necessary — is acceptable. Erring on the side of over-emit (marking unsafe packets actionable) is not.

-# Handoff: Honesty Hardening + TypeScript Must-Use Campaign Closeout
-
-Date: 2026-06-15
-Branch / PR: `docs/honesty-campaign-closeout` / pending at authoring
-Latest landed spec chain: `RIPR-SPEC-0103` … `RIPR-SPEC-0110`
-
-## Current Work Item
-
-`campaign/honesty-and-must-use`
-
-This campaign moved RIPR from "produces interesting evidence" to "produces
-**honest, actionable, self-enforcing** evidence across the fleet," and from a
-TypeScript *preview* lane to one that is **must-use for mainstream TypeScript**.
-It did not bump the crate version, publish, or change the published `0.9.0`
-support tiers; the release decision (likely `0.10.0`) is deliberately parked for
-an explicit human call.
-
-## What landed (by theme)
-
-### 1. The fake-`exposed` class — fixed fleet-wide, then made a standing gate
-The central adversary this campaign was a single recurring shape: **evidence
-credited to a seam it does not actually observe → a false `exposed` /
-`strongly_gripped` / `strong_oracle_observed` claim.** It recurred across
-analysis stages, across languages, and was even baked into a golden. Each
-instance was closed fail-closed, and then the *class* was turned into a standing
-invariant:
-
-```text
-identity-not-token (Python)              #1242 / #1244 / #1247 / #1253
-oracle-kind-vs-seam-family (TS)          RIPR-SPEC-0104  #1248
-wrong-kind exemplar nomination (Rust)    RIPR-SPEC-0103  #1243
-unwrap_err variant binding (Rust)        RIPR-SPEC-0106  #1252
-error_path needs a variant oracle (Rust) RIPR-SPEC-0107  #1254
-SideEffect observation guard (TS)        RIPR-SPEC-0098  #1236
-stage confidence caps the headline       RIPR-SPEC-0109  #1219-D #1258
---------------------------------------------------------------------
-THE CAPSTONE: evidence-promotion honesty meta-gate
-                                         RIPR-SPEC-0108  #1257
-```
-
-`cargo xtask check-evidence-promotion-honesty` (RIPR-SPEC-0108) pins a
-cross-language adversarial corpus (`fixtures/evidence-promotion-honesty-corpus/
-corpus.json`). It reads each charter fixture's pinned golden and asserts the
-class **independent of the golden** — so it catches a *dishonest re-bless* that
-plain `goldens check` would accept (because `goldens check` only asserts
-`binary == golden`). Every future fake-`exposed` fix registers a `cases[]` entry.
-The invariant + corpus + gate are shared; the per-language matchers are not
-unified (different taxonomies, different edge policies).
-
-### 2. TypeScript: preview → must-use for mainstream
-```text
-single-hop re-export test discovery       #1231
-package.json test-runner detection        #1233
-.toThrow('payload') exact-error oracle     RIPR-SPEC-0097 #1234
-tsconfig compilerOptions.paths aliases     RIPR-SPEC-0099 #1237 (opt-in, fail-closed)
-named import-alias owner-call credit       RIPR-SPEC-0102 #1241
-runner-disclosure honesty                  RIPR-SPEC-0101 #1240
-missing_actionability_fields self-fix      #1251
-advisory related-test codeLens             RIPR-SPEC-0100 #1238
-```
-End-to-end dogfood verdict: **must-use for mainstream single-package and simple
-monorepo TS, no over-claims found.** TypeScript remains preview/advisory tier;
-preview can be actionable when the full repair-packet contract holds, but it is
-delegatable, not gate authority. Remaining gap: namespace-import owner calls — a
-documented honesty-safe under-emit, not a release blocker.
-
-### 3. LSP cockpit: performance is part of honesty
-The LSP first-open ran the full-repo seam inventory (~336 s vs the CLI's ~14 s
-diff pass) — dead-on-arrival, so agents would act on no state. `RIPR-SPEC-0105`
-(#1250) defers the seam inventory off the interactive path and **discloses** it
-(`run_status: "seams_deferred"`, a `limited`-family value); the full pass runs on
-the explicit `ripr.refresh` command. A fast path may be partial only if the
-status says so.
-
-### 4. Rust usefulness (#1168, fully closed)
-Error-return seams with dedicated `unwrap_err` tests that pin the exact variant
-were falsely `weakly_gripped`. Slice 1 (#1243) kind-gated the exemplar; slice 2
-(#1252) recognizes the `unwrap_err`+`assert_eq!(err, Variant)` oracle and binds
-it to the matching seam variant — a sibling variant or a generic `is_err()` stays
-`weakly_gripped` (fail-closed).
-
-### 5. The receipt → outcome → route-quality loop (#1123)
-Found ~90% already built and honest. The one missing link — a real producer for
-receipt staleness/orphan detection — landed as `RIPR-SPEC-0110` (#1261):
-`ripr receipt check --ledger` cross-references the receipt's `canonical_gap_id`
-against the live gap set (`receipt_ok` / `orphan_receipt` / `receipt_gap_mismatch`,
-non-zero on a real problem; **`not_available` when no ledger — never `receipt_ok`**).
-
-## Durable learnings (detail in `docs/LEARNINGS.md`)
-
-- **The fake-`exposed` is one cross-language class, now a standing gate, not
-  whack-a-mole.** When you fix the same shape three times, enforce the property.
-- **Goldens can encode dishonesty.** A re-bless is a semantic act; the meta-gate
-  pins the expectation independent of the golden.
-- **Verify the artifact — and the harness.** Gates / tests / builder self-reports
-  are weak oracles; so is your own harness. A wrong binary path or a non-pinned
-  rustfmt manufactures false *negatives*. Run the absolute worktree binary + the
-  pinned toolchain; inject a unique marker to confirm your edits are in the binary.
-- **Fail-closed is directional.** Under-emit before over-emit; `not_available`
-  beats fake-zero; an unprovable stage caps confidence and cannot read as certain.
-- **Honesty is tested at the surface.** Internal dishonesty becomes visible when
-  projected (a finding contradicting its own evidence); usability is where honesty
-  is tested; performance is part of honesty.
-- **Dogfood is the highest-signal tool.** Every adversarial dogfood found real
-  bugs the gates missed and re-grounded the roadmap. A closed-corpus "0
-  false-`exposed`" measures the corpus, not the analyzer — construction, not
-  sampling, finds silent over-credit.
-- **Operating model:** scout (read-only) → adversarial spec → build → verify
-  myself → gate. The scout-before-build repeatedly resolved uncertainty cheaply
-  and caught spec holes before they shipped.

+# RIPR-SPEC-0269: Task/result/receipt schemas bind the selected-work portfolio basis
+
+Status: proposed
+
+Owner: test-infra
+
+Created: 2026-10-09
+
+Linked issues:
+
+- #1706 (parent: bind packets, issue lifecycle and burn-down to
+  portfolio-selected work identity; this spec implements the #1633 consumer
+  of delivery slice PR B — task/result/receipt schemas)
+- #1633 (the task/result/receipt consumer being migrated here)
+- #6864 / RIPR-SPEC-0244 (the shared selected-work identity schemas this
+  consumer reuses: `PortfolioBasisV1`, `SelectedWorkIdentityV1`, the sealed
+  law/route vocabulary and the identity law engine; referenced, never
+  duplicated)
+- #1704 / #1794 / RIPR-SPEC-0234 (the work-portfolio compiler whose
+  captured inputs the check corpus references)
+- #1692 (goals-portfolio migration epic)
+
+Support-tier impact:
+
+- None.
+- The result check is an offline typed validation over committed captured
+  bytes. It launches no agent, selects no work, claims nothing, authorizes
+  nothing, calls no provider, reads no live GitHub state, and writes only
+  `target/ripr/reports/work-result-check.{json,md}` plus stdout.
+
+Policy impact:
+
+- None. No new process, network or file-policy surface. The command
+  registers in the command mutability catalog as `report_only`; its
+  mutation-negative test pins the read-only boundary against the fixture
+  tree.
+
+## Problem
+
+#1706 PR A (RIPR-SPEC-0244) defined the shared selected-work identity and
+portfolio-basis contract but deliberately migrated no consumer. The #1633
+task/result/receipt train is the first consumer that must move: without a
+migrated schema, a result could still be accepted for another repository,
+an older portfolio snapshot, a different issue or action, a stale basis, an
+unrecorded worktree or a wrong exact head, recreating the singleton
+indirectly — one campaign pointer or one active-goal digest could keep
+deciding whose results count. PR B must make every packet/result bind the
+repository, the portfolio-snapshot identity, the basis head and the full
+selected-work identity it extends, and must fail stale/wrong input visibly
+with the exact recompile/reconcile route.
+
+## Behavior
+
+`cargo xtask work result check [--corpus <dir>] [--json]` loads the
+committed task-result corpus (default `fixtures/work_result_identity`) and,
+for each scenario, compiles the referenced captured portfolio directory
+with the unchanged RIPR-SPEC-0234 compiler into a `PortfolioBasisV1`, then
+runs the result law engine over each committed `WorkTaskResultV1` row.
+Human Markdown and JSON projections derive from one check DTO and agree on
+scenario, case and pass/fail counts; neither can strengthen the other.
+
+### WorkTaskResultV1
+
+Every result row binds, reusing the RIPR-SPEC-0244 DTOs rather than forking
+them: the result id, the repository, the compiled portfolio-snapshot
+identity, the basis SHA, the full `SelectedWorkIdentityV1` the result
+extends, the closed result-kind vocabulary (`context_compiled` |
+`task_dispatched` | `build_completed` | `verification_recorded` |
+`review_recorded`), the writer worktree when any, the exact reported head,
+the retained evidence references, and the legacy compatibility references.
+The schema has no repository-wide current/default campaign, no mutable
+agent assignment, no CI wait state and no progress percentage;
+`deny_unknown_fields` rejects any such addition.
+
+### Result laws and exact routes
+
+The embedded selection must satisfy every RIPR-SPEC-0244 identity law
+first — the shared engine runs inside the result check, so a result cannot
+smuggle in a packet the selection check would reject. The result-level
+laws then bind: a result naming another repository routes
+`recompile_basis`; a result binding another portfolio-snapshot identity is
+stale and routes `recompile_basis`; a recorded basis SHA that no longer
+matches the captured default-branch head routes `recompile_basis`; a
+reported head that does not match the selection's expected head routes
+`reconcile_head`; a claimed worktree the selection does not record in its
+overlaps routes `reconcile_resources`; an empty evidence list routes
+`reconcile_selection` (a result with no evidence reference is a claim, not
+a result). Legacy `legacy_active_goal_ref` /
+`legacy_current_work_item_ref` fields on a result resolve read-only to
+historical campaign references, emit migration posture, and grant no
+write, readiness, merge or closeout authority; an unresolvable legacy
+reference routes `reconcile_selection`.
+
+### Captured-input reuse
+
+The corpus references the committed RIPR-SPEC-0244 captured directories
+(`fixtures/work_portfolio/corpus` and
+`fixtures/work_selection_identity/captured/*`) by relative path; captured
+bytes are never duplicated, and scenario captured paths keep the same
+fail-closed resolution rules as the selection check (corpus-local first,
+then the repository `fixtures/` root; absolute, parent-relative and
+backslash spellings fail closed on every platform).
+
+### Fixture provenance coverage
+
+`fixtures/work_result_identity/provenance.json` binds every corpus JSON
+byte with SHA-256 in the RIPR-SPEC-0223 convention; unlisted fixture files
+fail closed, and provenance paths reject absolute, parent-relative and
+backslash spellings on every platform.
+
+### Legacy compatibility
+
+Legacy references are read-only compatibility state. They never promote
+readiness, proof, support or completion, and a result row that would
+authorize a writer from a legacy reference has no field to express it — the
+closed vocabulary and `deny_unknown_fields` keep it unrepresentable.
+
+## Required Evidence
+
+- The committed corpus `fixtures/work_result_identity/corpus.json` with all
+  five required scenarios and per-case pinned expectations.
+- `fixtures/work_result_identity/provenance.json` SHA-256 bindings,
+  recomputed fail-closed by `cargo xtask check-fixture-contracts`.
+- `cargo xtask work result check` passing on the committed corpus, with
+  byte-stable JSON output and a stable portable identity across runs.
+- `cargo test -p xtask work_result_identity` pinning the acceptance items
+  this slice can honestly pin.
+
+## Inputs
+
+- The committed task-result corpus (`corpus.json`) and the captured
+  portfolio directories it references under `fixtures/`.
+
+## Outputs
+
+- `work_result_check_view.v1` JSON and the derived Markdown on stdout and
+  under `target/ripr/reports/work-result-check.{json,md}`.
+
+## Acceptance Examples
+
+- A build result binding the issue `9105` `start_build` selection against
+  the canonical corpus passes with one member campaign reference, the
+  matching snapshot identity, the matching basis head and evidence refs.
+- The same result shape against the standalone captured variant passes for
+  issue `9106` with zero campaign references.
+- A repair result for issue `9101` binds the worktree `<root>/wt-9101` the
+  selection recorded and passes.
+- A result carrying `legacy_active_goal_ref: "campaign-rust-repair"`
+  passes read-only, emits migration posture, and grants no authority.
+- A result naming another repository, another portfolio snapshot, a stale
+  basis, a wrong reported head, an unrecorded worktree, an embedded action
+  that mismatches the portfolio candidate, no evidence reference, or an
+  unresolvable legacy ref each fails with the exact pinned law/route pair.
+- The human Markdown projection renders the same snake_case wire names as
+  the JSON projection; `Debug` spellings never appear.
+
+## Non-Goals
+
+- No claim, wave-planning, synthesis, issue-intake or burn-down migration:
+  #1635/#1647, #1634, #1636, #1644 and #1648 keep their current behavior
+  and land in later slices.
+- No portfolio candidate ranking (owned by #1704), no autonomous selection,
+  no agent spawning, no source edit, merge or closeout authority.
+- No live GitHub, label, issue-age or title-keyword input; committed
+  captured bytes are the only authority.
+
+Requirement-level v2 blocks and PR-local implementation slices belong in
+their respective authorities; do not duplicate their normative prose here.
+Acceptance of this document does not imply implementation, evidence, or
+support.
+
+## Test Mapping
+
+- `xtask/src/work_result_identity.rs::tests::work_result_identity_committed_corpus_five_scenarios_hold`
+- `xtask/src/work_result_identity.rs::tests::work_result_identity_wrong_inputs_fail_stale_or_wrong_input`
+- `xtask/src/work_result_identity.rs::tests::work_result_identity_embedded_selection_reuses_shared_laws`
+- `xtask/src/work_result_identity.rs::tests::work_result_identity_result_schema_has_no_singleton_fields`
+- `xtask/src/work_result_identity.rs::tests::work_result_identity_valid_results_bind_their_selections`
+- `xtask/src/work_result_identity.rs::tests::work_result_identity_legacy_refs_read_only_no_authority`
+- `xtask/src/work_result_identity.rs::tests::work_result_identity_human_and_json_projections_agree`
+- `xtask/src/work_result_identity.rs::tests::work_result_identity_deterministic_output`
+- `xtask/src/work_result_identity.rs::tests::work_result_identity_corpus_loader_fails_closed`
+- `xtask/src/work_result_identity.rs::tests::work_result_identity_committed_provenance_covers_every_corpus_byte`
+- `xtask/src/work_result_identity.rs::tests::work_result_identity_command_mutate_nothing_mutation_negative`
+- `xtask/src/work_result_identity.rs::tests::work_result_identity_basis_facts_for_corpus_authoring`
+
+## Implementation Mapping
+
+- `xtask/src/work_result_identity.rs` — result DTOs, the result law engine
+  (reusing the RIPR-SPEC-0244 engine for the embedded selection), corpus
+  runner, projections, command, provenance loader and fixture validator.
+- `xtask/src/work_selection_identity.rs` — `build_portfolio_basis`,
+  `check_packet`, `CaseEvaluation`, `corpus_root`,
+  `resolve_scenario_captured` and `selection_wire_name` widened to
+  `pub(crate)`; the selection law engine itself is unchanged.
+- `xtask/src/command.rs`, `xtask/src/dispatch.rs` — `work result check`
+  registration in the parser, dispatcher and the command catalog.
+- `xtask/src/fixture_contracts/mod.rs`, `xtask/src/reports/fixtures.rs` —
+  corpus validator registration and the manifest-only fixture exemption.
+
+## Metrics
+
+- `unit_test_pass_rate` over the `work_result_identity` test prefix.
+- Corpus expectation coverage: 5/5 scenarios, 14/14 pinned cases passing.

+# RIPR-SPEC-0270: Durable claims bind one selected item and the exact portfolio basis
+
+Status: proposed
+
+Owner: test-infra
+
+Created: 2026-10-09
+
+Linked issues:
+
+- #1706 (parent: bind packets, issue lifecycle and burn-down to
+  portfolio-selected work identity; this spec implements the #1635/#1647
+  consumer of delivery slice PR B — local and durable claims)
+- #1635 / #1647 (the claim-binding consumers migrated here)
+- #6864 / RIPR-SPEC-0244 (the shared selected-work identity schemas this
+  consumer reuses: `PortfolioBasisV1`, `SelectedWorkIdentityV1`, the sealed
+  law/route vocabulary and the identity law engine; referenced, never
+  duplicated)
+- #1704 / #1794 / RIPR-SPEC-0234 (the work-portfolio compiler whose
+  captured inputs the check corpus references)
+- #1692 (goals-portfolio migration epic)
+
+Support-tier impact:
+
+- None.
+- The claim check is an offline typed validation over committed captured
+  bytes. It launches no agent, selects no work, claims nothing, authorizes
+  no writer, calls no provider, reads no live GitHub state, and writes only
+  `target/ripr/reports/work-claim-check.{json,md}` plus stdout.
+
+Policy impact:
+
+- None. No new process, network or file-policy surface. The command
+  registers in the command mutability catalog as `report_only`; its
+  mutation-negative test pins the read-only boundary against the fixture
+  tree.
+
+## Problem
+
+#1706 PR A (RIPR-SPEC-0244) defined the shared selected-work identity and
+portfolio-basis contract but deliberately migrated no consumer. The #1635
+local-claims and #1647 durable-claims trains must bind one selected
+issue/work item/action and the exact portfolio basis. Without a migrated
+schema, claims could keep asserting repository-wide priority from one
+campaign pointer, a stale basis could silently release or hand over a
+writer, and one generic conflict resource could serialize unrelated work.
+PR B must make every claim bind exactly one selection and basis, must keep
+claiming one item from asserting repository-wide priority, and must route
+every stale basis and every resource conflict to reconciliation — never
+automatic release or takeover.
+
+## Behavior
+
+`cargo xtask work claim check [--corpus <dir>] [--json]` loads the
+committed durable-claim corpus (default `fixtures/work_claim_identity`) and,
+for each scenario, compiles the referenced captured portfolio directory
+with the unchanged RIPR-SPEC-0234 compiler into a `PortfolioBasisV1`, then
+runs the claim law engine over each committed `WorkClaimV1` row in order.
+Claims that pass join the scenario's committed claim set and constrain
+later claims. Human Markdown and JSON projections derive from one check DTO
+and agree on scenario, case and pass/fail counts; neither can strengthen
+the other.
+
+### WorkClaimV1
+
+Every claim row binds, reusing the RIPR-SPEC-0244 DTOs rather than forking
+them: the claim id (a durable identity, never a reusable label), the
+repository, the compiled portfolio-snapshot identity, the basis SHA, the
+full `SelectedWorkIdentityV1` the claim binds, the writer worktree the
+claim occupies, the closed claim-kind vocabulary (`writer`), and the legacy
+compatibility references. The schema has no repository-wide
+current/default campaign, no priority field, no mutable agent assignment,
+no CI wait state and no progress percentage; `deny_unknown_fields`
+rejects any such addition, so claiming one item can never assert
+repository-wide priority.
+
+### Claim laws, interactions and exact routes
+
+The embedded selection must satisfy every RIPR-SPEC-0244 identity law
+first — the shared engine runs inside the claim check. The claim-level
+laws then bind the repository (`recompile_basis`), the portfolio-snapshot
+identity (`recompile_basis`) and the basis head (`recompile_basis`). A
+stale basis keeps the claim recorded with state
+`stale_requires_reconcile`: it is not released and no other claim takes
+over its worktree. The occupied worktree must be recorded in the selection
+overlaps (`worktree_identity`/`reconcile_resources`). The interaction laws
+bind the claim set: a duplicate claim id fails
+(`subject_identity`/`reconcile_selection`); one worktree cannot serve two
+selections at once (`worktree_identity`/`reconcile_resources`); one
+selection cannot be claimed by two worktrees
+(`subject_identity`/`reconcile_selection`). Every conflict names the
+occupying claim and leaves it active — reconciliation is the only route,
+never release or takeover. Legacy `legacy_active_goal_ref` /
+`legacy_current_work_item_ref` fields on a claim resolve read-only to
+historical campaign references, emit migration posture, and grant no
+write, readiness, merge or closeout authority; an unresolvable legacy
+reference routes `reconcile_selection`.
+
+### Captured-input reuse
+
+The corpus references the committed RIPR-SPEC-0244 captured directories
+(`fixtures/work_portfolio/corpus` and
+`fixtures/work_selection_identity/captured/*`) by relative path; captured
+bytes are never duplicated, and scenario captured paths keep the same
+fail-closed resolution rules as the selection check.
+
+### Fixture provenance coverage
+
+`fixtures/work_claim_identity/provenance.json` binds every corpus JSON
+byte with SHA-256 in the RIPR-SPEC-0223 convention under the
+`work_claim_identity_provenance.v1` schema version; unlisted fixture files
+fail closed, and provenance paths reject absolute, parent-relative and
+backslash spellings on every platform.
+
+## Required Evidence
+
+- The committed corpus `fixtures/work_claim_identity/corpus.json` with all
+  five required scenarios and per-case pinned expectations.
+- `fixtures/work_claim_identity/provenance.json` SHA-256 bindings,
+  recomputed fail-closed by `cargo xtask check-fixture-contracts`.
+- `cargo xtask work claim check` passing on the committed corpus, with
+  byte-stable JSON output and a stable portable identity across runs.
+- `cargo test -p xtask work_claim_identity` pinning the acceptance items
+  this slice can honestly pin.
+
+## Inputs
+
+- The committed durable-claim corpus (`corpus.json`) and the captured
+  portfolio directories it references under `fixtures/`.
+
+## Outputs
+
+- `work_claim_check_view.v1` JSON and the derived Markdown on stdout and
+  under `target/ripr/reports/work-claim-check.{json,md}`.
+
+## Acceptance Examples
+
+- Writer claims for three distinct selections on three distinct worktrees
+  all pass and join the committed claim set.
+- A standalone selection with zero campaign references is claimable.
+- A claim occupying a worktree already claimed for another selection
+  fails `worktree_identity`/`reconcile_resources`, names the occupying
+  claim, and leaves it active.
+- A second claim on an already-claimed selection fails
+  `subject_identity`/`reconcile_selection` and leaves the first claim
+  active.
+- A claim recorded against a stale basis fails
+  `basis_identity`/`recompile_basis` and stays recorded as
+  `stale_requires_reconcile`; it is not released and its worktree is not
+  taken over.
+- A claim carrying `legacy_active_goal_ref: "campaign-rust-repair"`
+  passes read-only, emits migration posture, and grants no authority; a
+  mismatched legacy work-item ref fails
+  `legacy_compatibility`/`reconcile_selection`.
+- The human Markdown projection renders the same snake_case wire names as
+  the JSON projection; `Debug` spellings never appear.
+
+## Non-Goals
+
+- No task/result, wave-planning, synthesis, issue-intake or burn-down
+  migration: #1633 lands in RIPR-SPEC-0269, #1634/#1636/#1644/#1648 and
+  the #1637/#1649 adapters keep their current behavior and land in later
+  slices.
+- No claim enforcement against live worktrees: the check validates
+  committed corpus rows only and mutates no claim store.
+- No autonomous claim creation, release, takeover or agent assignment.
+- No live GitHub, label, issue-age or title-keyword input; committed
+  captured bytes are the only authority.
+

+# RIPR-SPEC-0271: Execution-wave planning partitions the selected candidate set over explicit resources
+
+Status: proposed
+
+Owner: test-infra
+
+Created: 2026-10-09

+Linked issues:
+
+- #1706 (parent: bind packets, issue lifecycle and burn-down to
+  portfolio-selected work identity; this spec implements the #1634 consumer
+  of delivery slice PR B — wave planning)
+- #1634 (the wave-planning consumer migrated here)
+- #6864 / RIPR-SPEC-0244 (the shared selected-work identity schemas this
+  consumer reuses: `PortfolioBasisV1`, `SelectedWorkIdentityV1`, the sealed
+  law/route vocabulary and the identity law engine; referenced, never
+  duplicated)
+- #1704 / #1794 / RIPR-SPEC-0234 (the work-portfolio compiler whose
+  captured inputs the check corpus references)
+- #1692 (goals-portfolio migration epic)
+
+Support-tier impact:
+
+- None.
+- The wave check is an offline typed validation over committed captured
+  bytes. It launches no agent, selects no work, claims nothing, admits no
+  wave, calls no provider, reads no live GitHub state, and writes only
+  `target/ripr/reports/work-wave-check.{json,md}` plus stdout.
+
+Policy impact:
+
+- None. No new process, network or file-policy surface. The command
+  registers in the command mutability catalog as `report_only`; its
+  mutation-negative test pins the read-only boundary against the fixture
+  tree.
+
+## Problem
+
+#1706 PR A (RIPR-SPEC-0244) defined the shared selected-work identity and
+portfolio-basis contract but deliberately migrated no consumer. The #1634
+wave-planning train must move off the singleton: without a migrated plan
+schema, a generic global `active-goal` resource could keep serializing
+unrelated work, one campaign pointer could keep deciding which waves may
+run, and incomplete plans could silently drop selected candidates or
+schedule the same exclusive resource in two waves at once. PR B must make
+every plan consume the complete selected candidate set and
+capacity/conflict facts, must remove the generic `active-goal` resource in
+favor of explicit resources, and must admit independent waves across
+campaigns when semantic/physical resources and capacity are disjoint.
+
+## Behavior
+
+`cargo xtask work wave check [--corpus <dir>] [--json]` loads the
+committed wave-planning corpus (default `fixtures/work_wave_identity`) and,
+for each scenario, compiles the referenced captured portfolio directory
+with the unchanged RIPR-SPEC-0234 compiler into a `PortfolioBasisV1`, then
+runs the wave law engine over each committed `WorkWavePlanV1` row. Human
+Markdown and JSON projections derive from one check DTO and agree on
+scenario, case and pass/fail counts; neither can strengthen the other.
+
+### WorkWavePlanV1
+
+Every plan binds, reusing the RIPR-SPEC-0244 DTOs rather than forking
+them: the plan id, the repository, the compiled portfolio-snapshot
+identity, the basis SHA, the complete selected candidate set (full
+`SelectedWorkIdentityV1` each), the declared writer capacity, the waves,
+and the legacy compatibility reference. The schema has no repository-wide
+current/default campaign and no generic goal resource;
+`deny_unknown_fields` rejects any such addition.
+
+### Explicit resource vocabulary
+
+A wave names only explicit resources: `campaign-record:<id>` (the id must
+be a recorded campaign), `portfolio-schema`, `spec-ledger`,
+`output-contract:<id>`, `issue:<n>`, `pr:<n>` and `worktree:<path>` (the
+path must be a captured local worktree). `portfolio-schema` and
+`spec-ledger` are read-only shared references: sharing them never
+serializes unrelated work. Every other resource is exclusive. The retired
+generic `active-goal` spelling — and every non-explicit shape — fails
+closed with `campaign_ref_identity`/`reconcile_resources` and names the
+explicit vocabulary.
+
+### Wave laws and exact routes
+
+Every embedded selection must satisfy every RIPR-SPEC-0244 identity law
+first — the shared engine runs inside the wave check, so a plan cannot
+smuggle in a packet the selection check would reject. The plan-level laws
+bind the repository, portfolio-snapshot identity and basis head (each
+`recompile_basis`). The wave-level laws then bind: wave membership (a wave
+names only selected candidates, `subject_identity`/`reconcile_selection`),
+coverage (every selected candidate is assigned to exactly one wave,
+`subject_identity`/`reconcile_selection`), per-wave capacity (a wave
+cannot exceed the declared writer capacity,
+`worktree_identity`/`reconcile_resources`), the resource vocabulary, and
+disjointness of exclusive resources across concurrent waves
+(`overlap_visibility`/`reconcile_resources`, naming both waves and the
+shared resource). Disjoint cross-campaign waves — disjoint exclusive
+resources, shareable read-only schema/ledger references, capacity within
+bounds — are admitted. Legacy `legacy_active_goal_ref` on a plan resolves
+read-only to a historical campaign reference, emits migration posture, and
+grants no write, readiness, merge or closeout authority.
+
+### Captured-input reuse
+
+The corpus references the committed RIPR-SPEC-0244 captured directories
+(`fixtures/work_portfolio/corpus`) by relative path; captured bytes are
+never duplicated, and scenario captured paths keep the same fail-closed
+resolution rules as the selection check.
+
+### Fixture provenance coverage
+
+`fixtures/work_wave_identity/provenance.json` binds every corpus JSON
+byte with SHA-256 in the RIPR-SPEC-0223 convention under the
+`work_wave_identity_provenance.v1` schema version; unlisted fixture files
+fail closed, and provenance paths reject absolute, parent-relative and
+backslash spellings on every platform.
+
+## Required Evidence
+
+- The committed corpus `fixtures/work_wave_identity/corpus.json` with all
+  six required scenarios and per-case pinned expectations.
+- `fixtures/work_wave_identity/provenance.json` SHA-256 bindings,
+  recomputed fail-closed by `cargo xtask check-fixture-contracts`.
+- `cargo xtask work wave check` passing on the committed corpus, with
+  byte-stable JSON output and a stable portable identity across runs.
+- `cargo test -p xtask work_wave_identity` pinning the acceptance items
+  this slice can honestly pin.
+
+## Inputs
+
+- The committed wave-planning corpus (`corpus.json`) and the captured
+  portfolio directories it references under `fixtures/`.
+
+## Outputs
+
+- `work_wave_check_view.v1` JSON and the derived Markdown on stdout and
+  under `target/ripr/reports/work-wave-check.{json,md}`.
+
+## Acceptance Examples
+
+- A plan partitioning the editor-ux and rust-repair selections into two
+  waves over disjoint exclusive resources is admitted, although both waves
+  share the read-only `portfolio-schema` and `spec-ledger` references.
+- The narrow single-agent issue `9202` gets its own single-selection wave
+  and is admitted while another campaign's wave stays active.
+- A plan whose waves share the exclusive `output-contract:preview-panel`
+  fails `overlap_visibility`/`reconcile_resources` naming both waves.
+- A wave naming the retired `active-goal` resource fails
+  `campaign_ref_identity`/`reconcile_resources` and names the explicit
+  vocabulary; a non-explicit shape fails the same way.
+- A plan with a stale basis fails `basis_identity`/`recompile_basis`; a
+  plan that leaves a selected candidate unassigned fails
+  `subject_identity`/`reconcile_selection` naming the candidate.
+- A wave scheduling more selections than the declared writer capacity
+  fails `worktree_identity`/`reconcile_resources`.
+- The human Markdown projection renders the same snake_case wire names as
+  the JSON projection; `Debug` spellings never appear.
+
+## Non-Goals
+
+- No claim, synthesis, issue-intake or burn-down migration: #1633 lands in
+  RIPR-SPEC-0269, #1635/#1647 in RIPR-SPEC-0270, and #1636/#1644/#1648
+  and the #1637/#1649 adapters keep their current behavior and land in
+  later slices.
+- No wave execution, scheduling or agent spawning; the check validates
+  committed plan rows only and admits no wave into any runtime.
+- No autonomous selection or campaign placement; plans consume the
+  candidate set the root selected.
+- No live GitHub, label, issue-age or title-keyword input; committed

+# RIPR-SPEC-0272: Context/work-item packets bind the selected-work portfolio basis
+
+Status: proposed
+
+Owner: test-infra
+
+Created: 2026-10-17
+
+Linked issues:
+
+- #1706 (parent: bind packets, issue lifecycle and burn-down to
+  portfolio-selected work identity; this spec implements the #1632 consumer
+  of delivery slice PR B — context/work-item packets)
+- #1632 (the context/work-item packet consumer being migrated here)
+- #6864 / RIPR-SPEC-0244 (the shared selected-work identity schemas this
+  consumer reuses: `PortfolioBasisV1`, `SelectedWorkIdentityV1`, the sealed
+  law/route vocabulary and the identity law engine; referenced, never
+  duplicated)
+- #1704 / #1794 / RIPR-SPEC-0234 (the work-portfolio compiler whose
+  captured inputs the check corpus references)
+- #1692 (goals-portfolio migration epic)
+
+Support-tier impact:
+
+- None.
+- The context check is an offline typed validation over committed captured
+  bytes. It launches no agent, selects no work, claims nothing, authorizes
+  nothing, calls no provider, reads no live GitHub state, and writes only
+  `target/ripr/reports/work-context-check.{json,md}` plus stdout.
+
+Policy impact:
+
+- None. No new process, network or file-policy surface. The command
+  registers in the command mutability catalog as `report_only`; its
+  mutation-negative test pins the read-only boundary against the fixture
+  tree.
+
+## Problem
+
+#1706 PR A (RIPR-SPEC-0244) defined the shared selected-work identity and
+portfolio-basis contract but deliberately migrated no consumer. The #1632
+context/work-item packet train still assumed an `active goal` content
+digest and one current work item: without a migrated schema, a packet
+could still be compiled for another repository, an older portfolio
+snapshot, a different issue or action, or a stale basis, and a packet
+could smuggle in a repository-wide portfolio dump or let one campaign
+pointer decide whose context counts. PR B must make every packet bind the
+repository, the portfolio-snapshot identity, the basis head and the full
+selected-work identity it compiles context for, must keep every carried
+reference relevant to that selection, and must fail stale/wrong input
+visibly with the exact recompile/reconcile route.
+
+## Behavior
+
+`cargo xtask work context check [--corpus <dir>] [--json]` loads the
+committed context-packet corpus (default `fixtures/work_context_identity`)
+and, for each scenario, compiles the referenced captured portfolio
+directory with the unchanged RIPR-SPEC-0234 compiler into a
+`PortfolioBasisV1`, then runs the packet law engine over each committed
+`WorkContextPacketV1` row. Human Markdown and JSON projections derive from
+one check DTO and agree on scenario, case and pass/fail counts; neither
+can strengthen the other.
+
+### WorkContextPacketV1
+
+Every packet row binds:
+
+- `packet_id` — a stable packet identity string.
+- `repository` — must equal the basis repository.
+- `portfolio_snapshot` — the compiled snapshot identity; another snapshot
+  is stale.
+- `basis_sha` — the captured default-branch head; another head is stale.
+- `selection` — the full `SelectedWorkIdentityV1` the packet compiles
+  context for (the RIPR-SPEC-0244 schema already forbids repository-wide
+  campaigns, agent assignment, CI wait state and progress percentages).
+- `scope` — a closed vocabulary: `selected_work_only` or
+  `selected_work_plus_relevant_overflow`. There is deliberately no
+  repository-wide scope.
+- `context_refs` — relevant campaign/spec/context references. Every entry
+  must name a campaign reference's id or source, an accepted requirement,
+  a spec ref, an implementation slice, or an overlap issue/PR/claim/
+  worktree identity of the bound selection.
+- `overflow_refs` — relevant overflow for the widened scope; each entry
+  must satisfy the same relevance rule. A `selected_work_only` packet
+  must not carry overflow.
+- `compiled_from` — retained artifact references the packet was compiled
+  from; an empty list is a claim, not a packet.
+- `legacy_active_goal_ref` / `legacy_current_work_item_ref` — read-only
+  compatibility references (see Legacy compatibility).
+
+A packet may select an issue with no campaign placement at all; campaign
+references are context, never permission.
+
+### Packet laws and exact routes
+
+The embedded selection must satisfy every RIPR-SPEC-0244 law first; the
+packet-level laws then bind the repository, the portfolio-snapshot
+identity, the basis head, the compiled artifacts, the bounded scope and
+the relevance of every carried reference. Each wrong identity is reported
+once with its exact route:
+
+| law | route | packet-level trigger |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `repository_identity` | `recompile_basis` | packet names another repository |
+| `basis_identity` | `recompile_basis` | packet binds another snapshot or a stale basis head |
+| `subject_identity` | `reconcile_selection` | packet compiled from nothing, or a selected-work-only packet carries overflow |
+| `campaign_ref_identity` | `reconcile_selection` | a carried context/overflow reference is not relevant to the bound selection |
+| `legacy_compatibility` | `reconcile_selection` | a legacy ref does not resolve read-only to the bound selection |
+
+Embedded-selection violations (subject, action, basis, head, worktree,
+campaign-ref, overlap and legacy laws) fire through the shared engine
+with their own exact routes.
+
+### Captured-input reuse
+
+The corpus never duplicates captured bytes: each scenario names a
+`fixtures/work_portfolio` corpus or a RIPR-SPEC-0244
+`fixtures/work_selection_identity/captured/` directory, and the packets
+embed the committed RIPR-SPEC-0244 selection rows by deep copy at author
+time (`author_corpus.py`). The default-branch head is
+`7cb64d60c9dd0dda59586e6b72dcdf150296a26f` for every referenced captured
+directory.
+
+### Fixture provenance coverage
+
+`fixtures/work_context_identity/provenance.json` binds the sha256 of
+`corpus.json`; `check-fixture-contracts` recomputes the digest in both
+directions and reruns the check, so drifted or unlisted corpus bytes fail
+closed.
+
+### Legacy compatibility
+
+`legacy_active_goal_ref` must resolve to a recorded campaign carried as a
+`historical` reference by the bound selection; `legacy_current_work_item_ref`
+must match the bound selection's issue identity. Both emit migration
+posture, resolve read-only, and grant no write, readiness, merge or
+closeout authority.
+
+## Required Evidence
+
+- Committed corpus: six scenarios, eleven pinned cases, sha256-bound
+  provenance, rerun by `check-fixture-contracts`.
+- Unit tests: `xtask/src/work_context_identity/tests.rs` (13 tests, all
+  prefixed `work_context_identity_`).
+- Mutation-negative: the command writes only
+  `target/ripr/reports/work-context-check.{json,md}`.
+
+## Inputs
+
+- `fixtures/work_context_identity/corpus.json`
+- referenced captured portfolio directories (read-only)
+- `fixtures/work_context_identity/provenance.json`
+
+## Outputs
+
+- `target/ripr/reports/work-context-check.json`
+- `target/ripr/reports/work-context-check.md`
+- stdout (Markdown, or JSON with `--json`)
+
+## Acceptance Examples
+
+- A packet for a one-campaign selection compiles and passes
+  (`context-01`).
+- Several related campaign references stay context, never permission
+  (`context-02`).
+- A standalone issue with no campaign placement compiles a valid packet
+  (`context-03`).
+- A repair packet binds the recorded PR, claim and worktree as relevant
+  overflow (`context-04`).
+- A narrow one-file issue stays single-agent despite active campaigns
+  (`context-05`).
+- An unresolvable legacy active-goal ref, an irrelevant carried reference,
+  a selected-work-only packet with overflow, an evidence-free packet, a
+  wrong repository and a stale basis head each fail with their exact
+  law/route pair (`context-06`).
+
+## Non-Goals
+
+- No packet compiles context for more than one selected transition.
+- No packet carries raw portfolio, issue or log dumps; references only.
+- No packet grants write, readiness, merge or closeout authority.
+- No autonomous selection, campaign placement, agent spawning, source
+  edit, merge or closeout.
+- No synthesis, intake, planning-disposition, burn-down or adapter
+  consumer migrates in this slice.
