+
+Support-tier impact:
+
+- None.
+- The synthesis check is an offline typed validation over committed
+  captured bytes. It launches no agent, selects no work, claims nothing,
+  authorizes nothing, calls no provider, reads no live GitHub state, and
+  writes only `target/ripr/reports/work-synthesis-check.{json,md}` plus
+  stdout.
+
+Policy impact:
+
+- None. No new process, network or file-policy surface. The command
+  registers in the command mutability catalog as `report_only`; its
+  mutation-negative test pins the read-only boundary against the fixture
+  tree.
+
+## Problem
+
+#1706 PR A (RIPR-SPEC-0244) defined the shared selected-work identity and
+portfolio-basis contract but deliberately migrated no consumer. The #1636
+root synthesis train still reported against one current work item: without
+a migrated schema, a synthesis could be produced for another repository,
+an older portfolio snapshot, a different issue or action, or a stale
+basis, could silently report a different transition than the one selected,
+or could hide a coverage gap behind green rows. PR B must make every
+synthesis bind the repository, the portfolio-snapshot identity, the basis
+head and the full selected-work identity it reports on, must keep the
+reported transition identical to the selected action, must surface every
+recorded gap as a named contradiction, and must fail stale/wrong input
+visibly with the exact recompile/reconcile route.
+
+## Behavior
+
+`cargo xtask work synthesis check [--corpus <dir>] [--json]` loads the
+committed root-synthesis corpus (default `fixtures/work_synthesis_identity`)
+and, for each scenario, compiles the referenced captured portfolio
+directory with the unchanged RIPR-SPEC-0234 compiler into a
+`PortfolioBasisV1`, then runs the synthesis law engine over each committed
+`WorkSynthesisV1` row. Human Markdown and JSON projections derive from
+one check DTO and agree on scenario, case and pass/fail counts; neither
+can strengthen the other.
+
+### WorkSynthesisV1
+
+Every synthesis row binds:
+
+- `synthesis_id` — a stable synthesis identity string.
+- `repository` — must equal the basis repository.
+- `portfolio_snapshot` — the compiled snapshot identity; another snapshot
+  is stale.
+- `basis_sha` — the captured default-branch head; another head is stale.
+- `selection` — the full `SelectedWorkIdentityV1` the synthesis reports
+  on (the RIPR-SPEC-0244 schema already forbids repository-wide
+  campaigns, agent assignment, CI wait state and progress percentages).
+- `reported_transition` — the selected lifecycle action reported; it must
+  match the bound selection's action, so a synthesis cannot silently
+  report a different transition than the one selected.
+- `acceptance_coverage` — rows over the bound selection's accepted
+  requirements and spec refs, each `covered`, `uncovered` or
+  `contradicted`. A synthesis with no rows reports nothing.
+- `contradictions` — every `uncovered` or `contradicted` row must be
+  named here, so a synthesis can never hide a gap.
+- `next_action` — the bounded next step for the already-selected work;
+  never an encoded new selection.
+- `derived_from` — retained artifact references the synthesis derives
+  from; an empty list is a claim, not a synthesis.
+- `reported_campaign_ref` — when present, must be one of the bound
+  selection's campaign references; a synthesis cannot silently switch
+  campaign.

+  compatibility references (see Legacy compatibility).

+issue; `deny_unknown_fields` rejects such additions at parse time.

+
+The embedded selection must satisfy every RIPR-SPEC-0244 law first; the
+synthesis-level laws then bind the repository, the portfolio-snapshot
+identity, the basis head, the reported transition, the coverage rows, the
+contradiction honesty, the bounded next action, the derived artifacts and
+the reported campaign reference. Each wrong identity is reported once with
+its exact route:
+

+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `repository_identity` | `recompile_basis` | synthesis names another repository |
+| `basis_identity` | `recompile_basis` | synthesis binds another snapshot or a stale basis head |
+| `action_identity` | `reconcile_selection` | reported transition differs from the selected action |
+| `subject_identity` | `reconcile_selection` | no coverage rows, a hidden uncovered/contradicted row, an empty next action or no derived artifacts |
+| `campaign_ref_identity` | `reconcile_selection` | the reported campaign ref is not one of the bound selection's campaign refs |
+| `legacy_compatibility` | `reconcile_selection` | a legacy ref does not resolve read-only to the bound selection |

+own exact routes.

+embed the committed RIPR-SPEC-0244 selection rows by deep copy at author

+`7cb64d60c9dd0dda59586e6b72dcdf150296a26f` for every referenced captured

+`fixtures/work_synthesis_identity/provenance.json` binds the sha256 of

+
+- None.
+- The plan check is an offline typed validation over committed captured

+Policy impact:
+
+- None. No new process, network or file-policy surface. The command
+  registers in the command mutability catalog as `report_only`; its
+  mutation-negative test pins the read-only boundary against the fixture
+  tree.

+## Problem
+
+#1706 PR A (RIPR-SPEC-0244) defined the shared selected-work identity and
+portfolio-basis contract but deliberately migrated no consumer. The #1646
+planning-disposition consumer still planned against ad-hoc state: a plan
+could silently target an unknown campaign, block work without naming the
+blocking contract, assert authority to replace or reorder the whole
+portfolio, or plan for an issue identity the captured portfolio does not
+record. This spec migrates that consumer onto the shared basis: every plan
+binds the repository, the compiled portfolio-snapshot identity, the basis
+head and the full selected-work identity it plans for, and planning stays
+read-only — it can never replace or reorder the portfolio.

+## Behavior
+
+`cargo xtask work plan check [--corpus <dir>] [--json]` validates committed
+`WorkPlanV1` rows against the same `PortfolioBasisV1` the RIPR-SPEC-0244
+selection check compiles from immutable captured inputs (default
+`fixtures/work_plan_identity`). The check reuses the shared law engine
+instead of forking one: each plan embeds the `SelectedWorkIdentityV1` it
+plans for, the selection laws run on the embedded packet first, and the
+plan-level laws then bind the plan row. Human Markdown and JSON projections
+derive from one check DTO and can never strengthen each other.

+### WorkPlanV1
+
+- `plan_id`, `repository`, `portfolio_snapshot`, `basis_sha` — the bound
+  identities: the plan must name the basis repository, the compiled
+  portfolio-snapshot identity and the captured default-branch head.
+- `selection` — the full `SelectedWorkIdentityV1` the plan plans for; the
+  RIPR-SPEC-0244 selection laws run on it before any plan-level law, so a
+  plan cannot smuggle in a selection the selection check would reject.
+- `disposition` — one closed RIPR-SPEC-0244 `WorkPlanDispositionV1` wire
+  name (`single_scoped_pr`, `multi_pr_campaign`,
+  `append_to_named_campaign`, `standalone_issue_work`,
+  `focused_tracker_only`, `already_planned`,
+  `blocked_by_contract_or_decision`,
+  `root_portfolio_decision_required`).
+- `target_campaign` — the campaign targeted by `multi_pr_campaign` /
+  `append_to_named_campaign`; it must be a recorded campaign, and no other
+  disposition may silently carry one.
+- `reorders_portfolio` — read-only planning cannot replace or reorder the
+  whole portfolio; a row asserting otherwise fails visibly.
+- `blocked_by` — the contract or decision blocking the work, required by
+  `blocked_by_contract_or_decision`.

+  plan derived from nothing is a claim, not a plan.

+  compatibility references resolving read-only to historical campaign
+  references; both emit migration posture and grant no write, readiness,
+  merge or closeout authority.

+agent assignment, no CI wait state and no progress percentage;
+`deny_unknown_fields` rejects additions, and no field on a plan grants
+write, readiness, merge or closeout authority.

+
+- The embedded selection must satisfy every RIPR-SPEC-0244 law first.
+- Repository identity: a plan for another repository is wrong input —
+  `repository_identity` → `recompile_basis`.
+- Portfolio-snapshot identity: a plan binding another snapshot is stale —
+  `basis_identity` → `recompile_basis`.
+- Basis identity: a recorded basis head that no longer matches the captured
+  default-branch head is stale — `basis_identity` → `recompile_basis`.
+- Read-only boundary: `reorders_portfolio: true` —
+  `subject_identity` → `reconcile_selection`.
+- Campaign target: a campaign-targeting disposition with no
+  `target_campaign`, with an unrecorded target, or a non-targeting
+  disposition carrying one — `campaign_ref_identity` →
+  `reconcile_selection`.
+- Blocked disposition: `blocked_by_contract_or_decision` with an empty
+  `blocked_by` — `subject_identity` → `reconcile_selection`.
+- Derived artifacts: an empty `derived_from` — `subject_identity` →
+  `reconcile_selection`.
+- Legacy compatibility: an unresolvable `legacy_active_goal_ref` or a
+  `legacy_current_work_item_ref` that does not match the bound selection's
+  issue — `legacy_compatibility` → `reconcile_selection`.

+

+

+active-goal packet attempting to authorize planning fails closed.

+## Problem

+#1706 PR A (RIPR-SPEC-0244) defined the shared selected-work identity and
+portfolio-basis contract but deliberately migrated no consumer. The
+#1637/#1649 Codex adapter still delegated against ad-hoc state: a
+subagent could be handed a prompt that re-read the whole portfolio instead
+of the selected-work context packet, a builder could be delegated without
+a prepared claim or isolated worktree, a subagent could be handed claim
+write authority that belongs in the root thread, or a delegation could
+bind an issue identity the captured portfolio does not record. This spec
+migrates that consumer onto the shared basis: every delegation binds the
+repository, the compiled portfolio-snapshot identity, the basis head and
+the full selected-work identity it delegates, with one closed project role
+and one closed flow stage.

+## Behavior
+
+`cargo xtask work adapter check [--corpus <dir>] [--json]` validates
+committed `WorkAdapterV1` delegation rows against the same
+`PortfolioBasisV1` the RIPR-SPEC-0244 selection check compiles from

+embeds the `SelectedWorkIdentityV1` it delegates, the selection laws run
+on the embedded packet first, and the adapter-level laws then bind the
+delegation row. Human Markdown and JSON projections derive from one check

+
+- `adapter_id`, `repository`, `portfolio_snapshot`, `basis_sha` — the
+  bound identities: the delegation must name the basis repository, the
+  compiled portfolio-snapshot identity and the captured default-branch
+  head.

+  subagent; the RIPR-SPEC-0244 selection laws run on it before any
+  adapter-level law, so a delegation cannot smuggle in a selection the
+  selection check would reject.
+- `role` — one closed project-role wire name: the six base execution
+  roles from #1637 (`scout`, `adversary`, `builder`, `verifier`,
+  `reviewer`, `cleanup_auditor`) plus the five issue-lifecycle roles from
+  #1649 (`issue_triager`, `spec_author`, `spec_adversary`,
+  `work_planner`, `burn_down_reviewer`).
+- `flow_stage` — one closed stage wire name (`reconstruct`, `select`,
+  `compile`, `delegate`, `claim_write`, `verify_review`, `reconcile`).
+- `subagent_reads_portfolio` — must stay `false`: a subagent consumes the
+  selected-work context packet plus relevant overflow on demand and never
+  re-reads the whole portfolio; portfolio compilation stays in the root
+  thread.
+- `result_schema` — the strict bounded result schema the delegation must
+  return (for example `SubtaskResult` or the typed issue/spec/plan/burn-down
+  result).
+- `derived_from` — retained artifact references the delegation derives
+  from; a delegation derived from nothing is a claim, not a delegation.
+- `legacy_active_goal_ref` / `legacy_current_work_item_ref` — legacy
+  compatibility references resolving read-only to historical campaign
+  references; both emit migration posture and grant no write, readiness,
+  merge or closeout authority.

+agent assignment, no CI wait state and no progress percentage;
+`deny_unknown_fields` rejects additions, and no field on a delegation
+grants write, readiness, merge or closeout authority.

+### Adapter laws and exact routes

+- The embedded selection must satisfy every RIPR-SPEC-0244 law first.
+- Repository identity: a delegation for another repository is wrong input

+  captured default-branch head is stale — `basis_identity` →
+  `recompile_basis`.
+- Subagent portfolio boundary (#1637): `subagent_reads_portfolio: true` —
+  `subject_identity` → `reconcile_selection`.
+- Write-capable roles (#1637 builder contract): a `builder` delegation
+  whose bound selection carries neither a prepared claim nor an isolated
+  worktree — `subject_identity` → `reconcile_selection`.
+- Claim boundary (#1635): a delegation at the `claim_write` stage —
+  `subject_identity` → `reconcile_selection`; subagents never claim, and
